section_7.description: Comparative framework for bridging communication gaps between Japanese expatriates/executives and Indian operational teams.

communication_dimensions.japanese_pattern: Implicit, high-context communication. Relies on 'Kuuki wo yomu' (reading the air), subtle cues, and unspoken expectations.
communication_dimensions.indian_pattern: Explicit, highly vocal, and expressive communication. Expects detailed verbal instructions and energetic discussion.
communication_dimensions.bridge_strategy: Convert implicit Japanese expectations into written, itemized Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and detailed checklists.

communication_dimensions.japanese_pattern: Nodding and saying 'Hai' indicates comprehension ('I hear you'), not necessarily agreement or approval.
communication_dimensions.indian_pattern: Nodding or saying 'Yes' often implies agreement to perform or a positive commitment.
communication_dimensions.bridge_strategy: Establish explicit confirmation protocols ('Do we agree on the scope?' vs 'Did you understand the statement?').

communication_dimensions.japanese_pattern: Consensus-driven ('Ringi' system) and thorough risk-aversion. Slow initial decision, rapid flawless execution.
communication_dimensions.indian_pattern: Hierarchical, rapid decision-making driven by executive authority and adaptiveness ('Jugaad'/agility).
communication_dimensions.bridge_strategy: Map out the decision timeline upfront. Explain the Ringi approval process clearly to Indian managers to manage expectations.

communication_dimensions.japanese_pattern: Expects immediate 'Ho-Ren-So' (Report, Inform, Consult) at the very first sign of deviation or risk.
communication_dimensions.indian_pattern: Tendency to solve problems independently before reporting, or withholding bad news until a fix is attempted.
communication_dimensions.bridge_strategy: Reframe early delay reporting as a professional strength rather than a failure; conduct regular non-punitive syncs.

communication_dimensions.japanese_pattern: Indirect feedback given privately; public criticism is strictly avoided to preserve harmony ('Wa').
communication_dimensions.indian_pattern: Direct feedback common; energetic debate and public recognition are valued motivators.
communication_dimensions.bridge_strategy: Praise in public, provide corrective feedback in private 1-on-1 meetings, focusing strictly on data and processes.

key_phrases_and_nuances.japanese_phrase: Zenshin shimasu / Sento shimasu (We will consider it)
key_phrases_and_nuances.actual_meaning: Polite non-committal or subtle 'No' / low feasibility.

key_phrases_and_nuances.indian_phrase: It will be done / Problem solved
key_phrases_and_nuances.perceived_by_japanese: The task is 100% completed and verified.
key_phrases_and_nuances.actual_meaning: The process has been initiated or an agreeable workaround has been identified.
